solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Made counterfeit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shaped or produced, as a smith hammers out metal or a bond is created
second meaning: faked, as a signature or banknote

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, 'made fake', but splits into two separate meanings of a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both shaped at a smithy or brought into being, and fraudulently copied like a signature or banknote.

clue.text: Separate books belonging to that woman

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
the possessive pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out the books that belong to a particular woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for something distinct or additional, apart from the thing already mentioned.

clue.text: Investigating racecourse condition on piebald horse — yielding softly

indicators.note: yielding means giving up, and softly is the musical piano mark, so the horse gives up that soft letter

parts.note: the going is the state of the turf at a racecourse, such as good or soft
a pinto is a horse with patches of white and another colour

explanation.surface: A racing tipster studies the state of the turf before backing a patchy-coated horse.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano, softly) comes off PINTO to leave INTO; in a down clue 'on' puts GOING above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Going into a matter is an idiom for examining or looking into it closely.

clue.text: Third of ancient folk raised to the surface in tomb

indicators.note: picks out the letter in position three, the one that will be moved
in a down entry, raising a letter to the surface lifts it to the very top, rearranging the order

parts.note: a plain synonym for very aged

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a third of an ancient people's remains lifted up out of a burial site.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the D, third letter of OLD MEN, rises to the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolmen is a prehistoric megalithic structure of upright stones topped by a slab, thought to have marked burial chambers.

clue.text: "Grate" bang out of order when overlooked in misspelling of "Great Britain"

indicators.note: a misspelling jumbles the letters of the phrase that follows
the letters of that word, in any order, are passed over and dropped from the longer phrase

explanation.surface: A pedant complains that a sign spelling the country's name wrongly really grates.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B, A, N and G from GREAT BRITAIN in whatever positions they sit, then rearrange the eight remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate on someone is to annoy or get on their nerves, the same as to vex them.

clue.text: Wearing suit, smooths pastries at irregular points

parts.note: dressed in, as in 'in a hat'
a suit or fit is a matching, as clothes fit a body

explanation.surface: A baker in a suit is smoothing the pastry at uneven spots.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads suit and smooths as nouns about a tailored baker, but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something happening in spurts with pauses, so irregularly from moment to moment.

clue.text: Stood up with bowl made of dark timber

parts.note: in the game of bowls, each ball is called a wood

explanation.surface: Someone got to their feet holding a bowl carved from dark wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A wood is a bowl in lawn bowls, the British game of rolling balls toward a small jack.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a reddish-brown tropical hardwood prized for furniture and musical instruments.

clue.text: Little bears this writer domesticated

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the first part holds the second inside it

parts.note: a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A small child carries this author's stuffed bears around, all tamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals but is the verb carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe an animal brought under human control, made gentle rather than wild.

clue.text: Drawers that go up lower body parts comprising wide design

indicators.note: to comprise is to include, so the body parts hold the other pieces

parts.note: digits at the bottom of the body
the cricket abbreviation for a wide ball

explanation.surface: Underpants are pulled up over the legs, cut to a broad pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawers' suggests underwear, but here it means things that draw, pulling gliders into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Tow planes are aircraft that haul gliders aloft on a cable, so they are pullers that climb.

clue.text: Moving seats in car, filth is all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that the car's seats are moving and dirt is everywhere inside.
explanation.definitionFit: These are ski-resort conveyances: chairs hung from a cable that carry riders uphill.

clue.text: Cut whingeing in conversation

indicators.note: in speech, so the word is judged by how it is said

explanation.surface: Someone sharply cuts off a person who keeps complaining while they chat.
explanation.walkthrough: Whingeing is British for whining or complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Mown is the past participle of mow, describing grass that has been trimmed.

clue.text: Scrap US college society infiltrated by FBI agents

indicators.note: something infiltrated has others slipped inside it

parts.note: a frat is an American student fraternity
G-men is slang for FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: Federal agents go undercover in an American fraternity and there's a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight but means a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a small broken-off piece, just as a fragment is a shard or bit.

clue.text: From behind, some beheld dawdler's rocking gait

indicators.note: reading from the back means right to left
only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Watching a slow walker from behind, you notice their swaying walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A waddle is the side-to-side walk of a duck, a swaying way of moving on foot.

clue.text: Scrutinise extremely satiric article

indicators.note: taken literally, at the extremes, so only the end letters are used

explanation.surface: A reader is told to examine a highly satirical piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for satiric, but it means the extremities.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over something carefully, examining it point by point.

clue.text: Beverage a comrade's drunk

indicators.note: an inebriated state, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink that a friend has knocked back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as the past participle of drink, fitting the beverage, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet vanilla-flavoured fizzy soft drink.

clue.text: Preventing nothing in cutting-edge technology leads to no good

indicators.note: the first piece is placed inside the next

parts.note: artificial intelligence is the current frontier of tech

indicators.note: the leading letters, first of each word, are taken

explanation.surface: Claims that leading-edge tech does nothing to stop bad outcomes.
explanation.walkthrough: Artificial intelligence is today's standard example of cutting-edge technology, and 'nothing' sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoiding something means steering clear of it, keeping it from happening, close to stopping it.

clue.text: Guide outsiders from Ireland around cleric's home

indicators.note: turned around, so the pair swap places
the outside letters, first and last, are taken

explanation.surface: Visitors from abroad are shown around an Irish priest's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a listing of names and addresses, a book that helps people find things.

clue.text: Whole tennis team's belief regularly lacking

indicators.note: dropping letters at a steady interval leaves every other one

parts.note: the even-placed letters, second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A tennis squad loses faith in itself from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a group or set taken together as one unit, all its parts combined.

clue.text: Group of soldiers knight had noted

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A regiment's knight had written something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' looks like 'wrote down' after 'had', but it is the adjective famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean well-known and celebrated, enjoying a wide reputation.

clue.text: Infatuation delivering constant feeling of euphoria

indicators.note: delivering in the sense of freeing from, so the word is relieved of a letter

parts.note: a crush is a passing infatuation
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A love affair brings a steady sense of elation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush is a sudden thrilling surge of pleasure or excitement, like a high.

clue.text: One transformed corporation from the bottom up supported by worker

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading upward runs the word backwards

parts.note: corporation is a jocular old word for a pot belly, a tum
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A company is reshaped from the ground up, propped up by its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a business, but it is old slang for a large stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutant is a living thing whose genes have changed, a being altered from its normal form.

clue.text: Deconstruction of poem is set as task

indicators.note: taking something apart lets it be rebuilt differently

explanation.surface: A literature teacher assigns pulling a poem apart as homework.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose a duty or burden is to lay it on someone as an obligation.

clue.text: Casino croupier finally cut deck

indicators.note: at the end, so the last letter of each word

parts.note: the final letters of the two words

explanation.surface: In a casino, the dealer at last cuts the deck of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a pack of cards but means a level on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, below the waterline.

clue.text: Prune nectar stripped guts out

indicators.note: out as in wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
stripping removes the outer layer, leaving the inner letters

explanation.surface: Someone eats a plum after the juice was removed and its insides scooped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prune' looks like the dried fruit, sitting near nectar, but it is the verb meaning cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune is to cut back or shorten, as to truncate is to lop off the end.

clue.text: Brief discussion about feature of kite

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is lopped

explanation.surface: A short chat about how a kite is made.
explanation.walkthrough: The kite here is the bird of prey, not the toy on a string.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a hooked claw, a characteristic part of a raptor such as a kite.

clue.text: Hood initially covering bird of prey

indicators.note: at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A falconer's hood is first placed over a raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a loose head covering, especially the large one on a monk's habit.

clue.text: Roughly rock, held in place by stark strain of gondolier

indicators.note: held by something means enclosed within it

parts.note: to sway from side to side

explanation.surface: A boatman sings in a harsh, rocking style while steadying the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' suggests effort, but it means a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarolle is a traditional Venetian boat song sung by gondoliers, so a strain or melody of theirs.

clue.text: Fish strikes, catching victim

indicators.note: to catch is to grab hold, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to lam is an informal verb meaning to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: A predator fish strikes, snaring its victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampreys are eel-like jawless fish with sucking mouths that latch onto other fish.

clue.text: Difficult hearing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tiresome, hard to put up with

definitions.note: a verb form: conducting a court hearing
definitions.meaning: second meaning: judging a case in court

explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult hearing' sounds like a deafness problem; a judge is hearing a case when trying it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both irksome and wearing, and putting someone on trial before a judge in court.
